```plato
//==
// # Mesh topology interfaces
//
// Three rungs of a ladder, each strictly stronger than the one below:
// counted mesh elements (IMeshElementCounts), which elements touch which
// (IMeshIncidence), and constant-time half-edge navigation (IHalfEdge).
// The derived functionality of all three lives in
// `meshes.library.plato`.
//
// The rungs exist because real representations sit on different ones. An
// indexed triangle soup can count vertices and faces; a face-vertex list can
// answer incidence queries but only by search; a built half-edge structure
// answers neighbourhood walks in constant time. Naming the middle rung is what
// lets connectedness — components, boundary loops, valence, manifoldness — be
// written once against the weakest representation that can support it.

// Anything with counted mesh elements: vertices, undirected edges, and faces
// (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polygon_mesh). This is a census, not
// connectivity: it says how many of each element there are and nothing about
// which touches which. That is still enough for the Euler characteristic and,
// on a closed connected manifold, the genus.
//
// UndirectedEdgeCount counts DEDUPLICATED undirected edges — one per pair of
// half-edges, not one per directed side and not one per face corner. A
// representation that cannot dedupe without building incidence should implement
// IMeshIncidence and derive the count from it rather than guess: an over-count
// silently corrupts every Euler-characteristic result.
interface IMeshElementCounts
{
    VertexCount(x: Self): Integer;
    UndirectedEdgeCount(x: Self): Integer;
    FaceCount(x: Self): Integer;
}
```
